content:
In LaTeX, `\rowcolor` is used to color an entire row in a table.

## Basic usage

You usually need one of these packages:

```latex
\usepackage[table]{xcolor}
```

Then inside a `tabular`:

```latex
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|}
\hline
\rowcolor{gray!30}
A & B \\
\hline
1 & 2 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
```

## Example

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage[table]{xcolor}

\begin{document}

\begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
\hline
\rowcolor{blue!20}
Col1 & Col2 & Col3 \\
\hline
a & b & c \\
\rowcolor{yellow!30}
d & e & f \\
\hline
\end{tabular}

\end{document}
```

## Notes

- `\rowcolor{color}` applies to the current row.
- Put it at the start of the row.
- You can use colors like:
  - `red`
  - `blue!20`
  - `gray!15`

## Alternating row colors

Use `\rowcolors`:

```latex
\usepackage[table]{xcolor}

\rowcolors{2}{gray!15}{white}
\begin{tabular}{|c|c|}
A & B \\
1 & 2 \\
3 & 4 \\
\end{tabular}
```

If you want, I can also show:
- how to use `\rowcolor` with `booktabs`
- how to color only one cell
- how to fix common `\rowcolor` errors
